title: First frame is 159.1 kB gz vs ADR 0095's 125 kB; closing it is an owner call
body:
## Summary
The first frame of Main loads 159,082 B of gzipped JavaScript in 12 chunks; ADR 0095 records about 125 kB (shared chunk 97 + console 27), so the build is about 34 kB over the record. The new byte gate holds today's figure; it does not close the gap.

## Description
`apps/desktop/scripts/first-paint.mjs` (commit 27810da) now measures the first frame from a production build and `apps/desktop/scripts/first-paint.test.ts` fails above a 161,000 B ratchet. The record it answers to says otherwise: `docs/adr/0095-the-cutover-deletes-the-bar-and-the-old-views-and-the-first-paint-is-a-budget.md:28` "about 125 kB gzipped to draw the first frame (the shared chunk 97 kB, the console 27 kB)", `docs/redesign/parity.md:120` "first-paint JS is about 125 kB gzipped (app 97 + console 27), pinned by console/graph.test", and the overlay `.claude/scan-sweep/config.md` "First paint (about 125 kB gz) is pinned by console/graph.test.ts". Today: app 121.1 kB, root 26.7 kB, ten small chunks 11.3 kB. The shared `app` chunk grew about 24 kB past the record. Which way to close it is a product and architecture choice: split the shared chunk so depth-only code leaves it (page-load-pipeline/script-cost-is-main-thread-time), or re-record the budget at the measured figure with a reason. The prompt that built the gate forbade raising or rewriting the ADR's figure from a sweep.

## Flow
- owner reads the chunk breakdown (`node -e` over `measureFirstPaint` on any build, or the gate's failure message)
- either: attribute the app chunk's 121 kB by module (rollup visualizer or a manifest walk) and move what the first frame does not draw behind `import()`, lowering `FIRST_PAINT.ceilingBytes` as it drops
- or: a later ADR re-records the budget at the measured figure, and parity.md and the overlay stop saying graph.test pins bytes

## Expected impact
The record and the gate agree; either the first frame gets ~34 kB lighter (less parse on cold start in WebView2) or the record stops claiming a figure the tree does not meet. Could break: a chunk split can move a module the first frame does need behind a network-free but async import, adding a frame of delay.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - the first frame meets the recorded 125 kB budget
Before: 159,082 B gzipped, 12 chunks (production build 2026-10-16, gzip default level)
After: not built - the direction (split vs re-record) is the owner's
Method: gate - the first-paint test measures it on every `pnpm test`; the change itself is a direction call
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
evidence:
apps/desktop/scripts/first-paint.test.ts red at a 158,000 B ceiling: "first paint is 159.1 kB gzipped, over the 158.0 kB ceiling (largest: assets/app-_zlknGaR.js 121.1 kB, assets/root-CvGYM3TN.js 26.7 kB, assets/voice-setup-Dj-3iEJw.js 3.4 kB)"
docs/adr/0095-...md:28-29 "about 125 kB gzipped to draw the first frame (the shared chunk 97 kB, the console 27 kB), from 780 kB"
docs/redesign/parity.md:120 "first-paint JS is about 125 kB gzipped (app 97 + console 27), pinned by console/graph.test"
.claude/scan-sweep/config.md "First paint (about 125 kB gz) is pinned by console/graph.test.ts"

title: Frozen daemon is built without keyring, so source and shipped seals split
body:
## Summary
The documented sidecar build (`uv sync --extra build`) removes the `connectors` extra, so a frozen daemon is built without `keyring` and seals connector credentials with DPAPI, while a source daemon run with the extra seals them in the keystore; neither can read the other's.

## Description
`scripts/build-sidecar.py:3` and `apps/desktop/SIDECAR.md:96` say `uv sync --extra build`; `uv sync` is exact and uninstalls packages of extras not named, so `keyring` (the `connectors` extra, pyproject.toml) leaves the environment PyInstaller freezes. `src/athena/connectors/seal.py:176` imports keyring lazily and `select_seal` (seal.py:204-223) falls back to DPAPI on Windows. `src/athena/connectors/vault.py:798` writes the seal kind into each record but `vault.py:290` picks the seal by availability, not by the record, so a token sealed under keyring by `uv run athena serve` is looked up in DPAPI by the shipped binary and reads as absent (and the reverse). The build prints nothing about which optional extras it froze. packaging/adoption-time-packaging-audit: "a dependency works in the dev process and dies in the packaged binary". Fixed: the build names the extras it needs (`uv sync --extra build --extra connectors`) and refuses or warns when `keyring` is not importable; the vault reads a record with the seal its record names, or says which seal it needs.

## Flow
- `uv sync --extra connectors`; `uv run athena serve`; connect Gmail -> record seal "keyring"
- `uv sync --extra build`; build the sidecar; start the shell with it -> vault selects DPAPI -> the Gmail token is not found -> "not connected"
- fix order: build-sidecar.py checks `importlib.util.find_spec("keyring")` and prints the seal the binary will use (or refuses); SIDECAR.md names both extras; a vault test that a record sealed under one kind is reported, not silently absent, when that seal is unavailable

## Expected impact
A person who switches from the dev loop to the installed app keeps their connections, or is told why not. Could break: refusing the build without keyring would stop a machine that deliberately ships DPAPI; warn first.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the frozen and source daemons seal the same way, or say they do not
Before: walked: `uv sync --extra build` removes keyring (uv exact sync), select_seal falls back to DPAPI, vault ignores the record's seal kind
After: build prints the seal; the vault reports a record whose seal is unavailable
Method: simulation - three walked steps; the round may not run PyInstaller, and the vault is the connector-service context's
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
pyproject.toml: build = ["pyinstaller>=6.10"]; connectors = ["keyring>=25"]
apps/desktop/SIDECAR.md:96 uv sync --extra build
src/athena/connectors/seal.py:176 import keyring (lazy); :218-221 with suppress(SealUnavailable): return KeyringSeal() ... return DpapiSeal(root)
src/athena/connectors/vault.py:290 self._seal = seal or select_seal(...); :798 rec.seal = self._seal.kind
instrument: a vault test sealing a record under 'keyring' and reading it with only DPAPI available (expected: a named reason, not 'absent'), plus a build-sidecar check of find_spec('keyring') with its printed seal

title: UAT driver passes a run with no expect() and drops a timed-out wait's error
body:
## Summary
`uat/driver/drive-script.mjs` exits 0 ("ran and every expect() passed") for a step script that called no `expect` at all, and `waitUntil` throws "timed out waiting for X" without the error the condition last threw.

## Description
`uat/driver/drive-script.mjs:89` sets exit 2 only when `checks.some((c) => !c.ok)`; a script whose checks array is empty (a typo'd call path, an early `return`, a step that only crops) writes `"code": 0` to its journal and reads as a pass. test-harness's failure-not-empty-success law: an empty verdict is not a passing one. `waitUntil` (:62-70) stores the last thrown error in `last` and then throws `timed out waiting for ${label}` without it, so a condition that failed because `athena` was undefined (no CDP page matched) reads the same as one that was merely slow. The verdict and the wait are inline after a top-level `connectOverCDP`, so neither can be tested without a running app. Fixed: the verdict and `waitUntil` move into a pure module the driver imports, with a node test; zero checks becomes its own exit code (or a journal flag), and the timeout names its last error.

## Flow
- `node uat/driver/drive-script.mjs run j1 <<< "await sleep(10)"` against the app -> journal code 0, checks []
- a wait on `athena.evaluate(...)` with no athena page -> "timed out waiting for X" (the TypeError is lost)
- build: `uat/driver/verdict.mjs` (verdict(checks, threw), waitUntil with last error) + `node --test` file; then the driver's exit code for zero checks, which the uat skill's driver section must also state

## Expected impact
A journey that checked nothing stops reading green, and a timed-out wait says why. Could break: journeys that intentionally only capture crops would need one `expect`, or the skill's verdict table a new code.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a UAT run's exit code means something was checked
Before: zero-check script -> code 0 (read at drive-script.mjs:79-89); timeout message omits `last` (:69)
After: zero-check -> a distinct code; timeout message carries the last error
Method: simulation - the verdict is inline after a CDP attach, and the round may not run the driver against the app; the instrument is the pure module
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: uat/driver/verdict.mjs exporting verdict(checks, threw) and waitUntil, with a node --test file: zero checks -> non-zero, a timeout message containing the last thrown error; the uat skill's driver section is outside the round's write set (never-touch) and needs the same exit-code line

title: The preview harness and its fixtures ship inside the Tauri bundle
body:
## Summary
`vite.config.ts` builds `preview.html` into the same `dist/` Tauri packages, so the installed app carries the module preview harness: 7 files reachable only from it, 233.9 kB raw (54.4 kB gz).

## Description
`apps/desktop/vite.config.ts:9-12` makes `preview.html` a build input on purpose ("a harness that is not built is a harness that has already rotted"), and `scripts/perf-gate.mjs` serves it from a production build. `apps/desktop/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json:7` packages the whole of `dist/` (frontendDist, built by `pnpm build`, :10), so the shipped app holds a page that renders fixtures with no daemon, under the privileged `tauri://localhost` origin. A probe over a fresh build walked static and dynamic imports from chrome, athena and halo against preview: 7 files only preview reaches (preview-*.js 163 kB and six view-*.css). packaging/native-payload-verification: "shipped tree holds files no manifest explains". Fixed: preview stays an input for `pnpm build` and the perf gate, and drops out when the Tauri CLI drives the build (it sets `TAURI_ENV_*`), with a test over the build output under that env.

## Flow
- `pnpm build` -> dist/preview.html + assets/preview-*.js; `tauri build` packages dist/ -> the installer carries them
- fix: `input` omits preview when `process.env.TAURI_ENV_PLATFORM` is set; a vitest case builds with it set and asserts no preview.html
- verify: one `tauri build` and a listing of the bundled frontend

## Expected impact
About 234 kB less in the installer and no fixture page in the shipped origin. Could break: anything that navigates the shell to preview.html in a packaged build (none found by grep).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the shipped bundle carries only what the app loads
Before: 7 preview-only files, 233.9 kB raw / 54.4 kB gz in a production build (probe 2026-10-16)
After: 0 under a Tauri-driven build (not built)
Method: probe - the closure walk over a real build; the After needs a Tauri build, outside this round
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
probe preview-only.mjs over a production build: { previewOnlyFiles: 7, rawKB: '233.9', gzKB: '54.4' } - preview-6OiVg-5N.js preview-C3hh6BLT.css view-BNvrHjVk.css view--92E6b3z.css view-DKpKGhLe.css view-tsrsxQt8.css view-hZCtb4s_.css
apps/desktop/vite.config.ts: input { chrome, athena, preview, halo }
instrument: a vitest build with TAURI_ENV_PLATFORM set asserting no preview.html in the output, plus one `tauri build` listing the packaged frontend
